answer: One defense is entropy-priced admission. Each new identity's entry bond scales with how closely its funding trail and behavior match agents already on the ledger: a faint whisper of correlation is tolerated, but near-duplicates climb a steep curve. An honest agent sits at a lone vertex paying the floor, while a sybil fleet piles clones into one dense cluster whose shared fingerprint drives each marginal bond toward the zenith. Holding N near-identical identities then costs roughly N squared, not N, so faking a crowd is quadratically expensive while real diversity stays cheap.
